models.name: Model-Lumen-RANS (MLR)
models.what_it_computes: Steady incompressible RANS of the catheter’s internal lumen and side ports to predict pressure drop versus flow, wall shear stress, and entrance/exit loss coefficients under prescribed flow rates.

models.name: Model-Nav-NarrowGap (MNNG)
models.what_it_computes: Transient CFD in the pericatheter narrow gap using lubrication approximations within tortuous vessel geometries to estimate hydrodynamic drag during advancement, near-wall shear at contact, and pressure fields influencing trackability.

mechanisms.name: Tortuous-path bending and torsion during navigation
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Resistance to advancement and steering through compound curvatures drives the push force required and the risk of buckling or loss of tip control (trackability).

mechanisms.name: Guidewire–catheter sliding friction within the distal lumen
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Friction along the wire–lumen interface modulates deliverability and can dominate incremental push force in tight anatomies (trackability).

mechanisms.name: Lumen viscous pressure drop under steady infusion
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Viscous losses set the flow resistance and affect achievable infusion rates and upstream pump pressures (flow resistance).

mechanisms.name: Entrance/exit losses and side-hole mixing under pulsatile delivery
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Unsteady local losses and port interactions add to mean pressure drop and influence jet patterns relevant to hemolysis and drug dispersion (flow resistance).

deviation.detail: All credibility factor scores are reported on a 0–12 numeric scale defined for this study (0 = no credible evidence; 12 = compelling, decision-grade evidence).

expected_decision.outcome_source: With these guardrails, the models provide reliable support for preclinical design control and contribute to a transparent, quantitative engineering rationale for catheter performance.

datasets: bench flow-loop measurements of pressure–flow relations across catheters and wire sizes
pulsatile injection tests for entrance/exit loss characterization and side-hole interaction effects
tortuous-phantom navigation tests capturing push force and torsional response
specialized tests in a short bench setup where a 60 mm distal segment with a wire inserted was driven at relative speeds 1–10 mm/s while fluid was infused at 10–50 mL/min
requirements: the trackability index measured in tortuous phantoms is computed as the mean push force required to achieve steady advancement at 10 mm/s through a standardized path, adjusted for rotational compliance
the flow resistance threshold is defined as the maximum allowable pressure drop at the proximal luer at specified flow rates

for a design variant to be advanced without additional bench configurations, the model must under-predict resistance by at least a 10% margin or over-predict drag by at least a 10% margin in the validated envelope, ensuring conservatism

expected_context_of_use: Context of Use (CoU): CFD predictions will be used to support design selection and design verification for catheter trackability and flow resistance across specified bench test conditions representative of indicated coronary and peripheral anatomies; results will inform test matrix reduction and acceptance rationales, not clinical decisions.

findings.mechanism: Lumen viscous pressure drop under steady infusion
spans: MLR predictions of total pressure drop achieved a mean absolute percent error (MAPE) of 3.1% across 96 operating points, with a maximum absolute error of 7.2% at 200 mL/min for the 0.018 in. lumen with 0.018 in. wire (expected near-annular flow).

findings.mechanism: Tortuous-path bending and torsion during navigation
spans: Inputs to MNNG include the gap profile h(s,θ) (constructed from nominal shaft outer diameter, conduit inner diameter, and manufacturing tolerances; contact is introduced where shaft–conduit interference occurs due to curvature-induced ovalization or manufacturing variability), the imposed advancement speed (1–20 mm/s in tests, default 10 mm/s), the fluid viscosity (3.0–4.0 mPa·s at 37 °C), and the boundary pressure at the distal end (set to ambient for open-tip or elevated for partial occlusion scenarios).

For navigation, centerline-derived paths were distilled into a curvature–torsion library: 12 coronary paths with peak curvature 6 catheter performance 0.8–1.3 cm1 and torsion 0.5–0.9 cm1; 8 peripheral paths with peak curvature 0.3–0.7 cm1 and torsion 0.1–0.4 cm1.
findings.span: Inputs to MNNG include the gap profile h(s,θ) (constructed from nominal shaft outer diameter, conduit inner diameter, and manufacturing tolerances; contact is introduced where shaft–conduit interference occurs due to curvature-induced ovalization or manufacturing variability), the imposed advancement speed (1–20 mm/s in tests, default 10 mm/s), the fluid viscosity (3.0–4.0 mPa·s at 37 °C), and the boundary pressure at the distal end (set to ambient for open-tip or elevated for partial occlusion scenarios).
